critique.problem: The title says center-based rehab caused better attendance, but patients chose their program, so the bars can only show that center-based attendance was higher, not why; in Q1 the two programs were 1 point apart.
critique.repair: Use a descriptive title that states what the bars show without a cause: attendance fell from Q1 to Q2 in both programs, more in the home-based one.

critique.problem: The y-axis starts at 76%, so in Q2 the center-based bar (80%) is drawn four times as tall as the home-based bar (77%) even though the gap is only 3 points.
critique.repair: Start the y-axis at zero with set_ylim(0, 100), so each bar's length is proportional to its value.

critique.problem: The y-axis has no label, so readers cannot tell that the numbers are the percentage of scheduled sessions patients attended.
critique.repair: Label the y-axis Scheduled sessions attended (%), label the x-axis Quarter, and write each value on its bar.

critique.problem: Only red versus green tells the programs apart, a pair many colorblind readers cannot distinguish and one that disappears in grayscale, because every bar has the same hatch.
critique.repair: Use colorblind-safe orange and blue and give each program its own hatch: dots for home-based and stripes for center-based.

critique.problem: Thick black edges, a heavy dark grid, and the same cross-hatch on every bar carry no data and pull attention away from the bar heights.
critique.repair: Drop the thick edges and the grid, hide the top and right spines, and keep hatches only where they mark the program.

question: How did the share of patients meeting the weekly exercise goal change across the four follow-up visits in each program?
audience: The rehab program coordinator, who will use it to decide where to add follow-up support.
intended_claim: Both programs improved from visit 1 to visit 4, and by visit 4 more Center-based patients met the goal than Home-based patients, 79% against 70%.
y_measure: Percentage of patients seen at the visit who met the weekly goal of 150 minutes of exercise (%)
grain: One row of the plotting table and one point on a line is one program at one follow-up visit.
text_alternative: Line chart of the percentage of patients meeting the weekly goal of 150 minutes of exercise (y-axis, %) at four follow-up visits (x-axis, visits 1 to 4) for the Home-based and Center-based rehab programs. Both rise across the visits: Home-based from 58% to 70% and Center-based from 57% to 79%, so the programs start about equal and Center-based finishes 9 points higher at visit 4, 79% against 70%. Patients chose their program, so the gap does not show that center-based rehab causes more exercise, and each percentage covers only the patients seen at that visit, about 45 per program, so a 9-point gap could also come from chance or from who returned.
